_about: THE ART OF MISSION 2's TWO NEW UNITS (Track M2U, 2026-10-11): the MOBILE ANTI-AIRCRAFT GUN (silhouette mobile_aa) and the MILITARY COMPLEX (silhouette military_complex), generators in scripts/ui/unit_marker_art_mobile_aa.gd and scripts/ui/unit_marker_art_static.gd, judged on the boards variants/mobile-aa/ and variants/military-complex/ (scripts/ui/boards/). EVERYTHING HERE IS PROPOSED by Track M2U; nothing is chosen (Alex picks a look from the board; his pick replaces default_look with a decision id and is logged in data/decisions/decisions.json). Each unit has three LOOKS, the unit sheet's way of having variants: a look is a generator plan (the sheet's genPlane kinds 'light', 'heavy', 'bomber' are the same idea), and the sheet's variant index (ui.json unit_art.variant) would select one; until ui.json lists these silhouettes the DEFAULT_LOOK below is the working default. Numbers: metres, degrees; a pair [lo, hi] is the range the seeded generator draws a parameter from (the unit sheet's R2 rounding), so the same seed makes the same vehicle or compound every run. Colours are ROLES resolved from the palette by scripts/render/ink_roles.gd, never hex: hue stays reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents; lightness is a ramp off paper; material is linework. The sheet's UNITS list has no entry for either unit yet (the sheet is a reference mockup, not edited): the seed indices continue it, 7 and 8 (0-6 are the sheet's).

sheet_index._reason: the next index in the unit sheet's seed rule (unitSeed(index, variant)): the sheet has 0 light fighter, 1 heavy fighter, 2 bomber, 3 tank, 4 battery, 5 small cruiser, 6 radio tower

default_look._reason: Alex 2026-10-11: 'I like the half track with quad Mount' (variants/mobile-aa, look 0). Earlier working-default reason: the half-track with a quad mount. It is the one that reads least like the tank (a narrow hull with a long open gun bed and wheels at the front) and is nearest to the sheet's tank in method, and a half-track is the 'tracked or half-tracked chassis' the brief asked for

looks.title: Half-track with a quad mount
looks.about: The narrowest and longest of the three: a cab and bonnet over two front wheels, two short tracks at the back, and an open gun bed with a four-barrel mount whose barrels are drawn raised and foreshortened over the cab. The accent is a recognition panel on the cab roof.

looks.title: Tracked hull with an open twin turret
looks.about: The nearest to the tank: a wide tracked hull with the engine deck at the back, but the turret is an open-topped eight-sided tub with the crew's heads in it, and the weapon is a pair of barrels drawn raised and foreshortened with flash hiders. The accent is the engine-deck panel, as on the tank.

looks.title: Light carrier with a ring mount
looks.about: The battery that moves: a short tracked carrier with a cab block at the front and a flat rear deck holding a round armour ring (the battery's sandbag ring in steel) round a pedestal mount with twin barrels, with ammunition crates beside it. The accent is a panel on the deck behind the ring.

sheet_index._reason: the next index after the mobile gun's 7 in the unit sheet's seed rule

default_look._reason: Alex 2026-10-11: 'And the hanger yard' (variants/military-complex, look 0). Earlier working-default reason: the hangar yard. It is the one with the most distinct silhouette at the planning zoom (one big barrel-roofed hall with a pale apron and round fuel tanks) and the one a bombing run most plausibly attacks

footprint_m._reason: the lead's brief: for example 80 x 60 m; the fence is drawn 4 m inside this and the buildings inside the fence, so the whole picture, shadows aside, fits the number the sim has as size_m (80, the long side)

map_scale_factor._reason: a static TARGET drawn at the MAP's scale (the brief; like a bridge, scenery with a unit's behaviour), not at the planes' scale. The marker layer draws a marker at the plane rule (a light fighter 36 px across, 4 px per metre at zoom 1) and nothing else changes that for a unit that is not in STATICS (the tower and the batteries are also doubled by marker.static_scale, 2). The map is 2 px per metre at zoom 1, so the complex's geometry is drawn at 0.5 of the marker's scale: 2 px per metre at zoom 1, 0.78 at the planning zoom 0.35 (the planes' 14 px floor keeps the marker rule from falling under 1.56 px/m, so the complex sits a little above the map's 0.7 there and stays that size below it, as a plane does). A different plane rule (data/scenarios sandbox view.plane_px, or a smaller smallest-unit) moves this number

heights_m._reason: building heights for the cast shadows (the shadow is as long as height x 0.97 at the map's sun): a hangar 11 m to the crown of its roof, a factory hall 9 m, a shed 4.5 m, a barracks range 5.5 m, a fuel tank 6 m, the chimney 26 m, a watch tower's platform 8 m. The village's house is 0.9 x its size (about 12 m footprint); these are taller, as industrial buildings are

fence_h_m._reason: chain link and wire; it casts a thin broken shadow only on the board's request, not in the mask: see-through

looks.title: Hangar yard
looks.about: A big barrel-roofed hangar on a pale concrete apron in the north of the fence, two sheds and two round fuel tanks, trucks in the packed-earth yard, a gatehouse on the south fence, and watch towers at two corners. The accent is a recognition panel on the hangar roof.

looks.title: Works with a saw-tooth hall
looks.about: A long factory hall with a saw-tooth roof (a shaded strip and a lit strip, repeated), a tall chimney whose long shadow is the tell at the planning zoom, a boiler house, a coal heap and three long sheds, inside a wire fence with a gate on the west. The accent is a recognition panel on the hall's roof.

looks.title: Barracks and depot
looks.about: Three long barracks ranges round a three-sided yard, a depot shed closing the fourth side, with a flagpole, parked vehicles and stacked crates, inside a low wall (the village's compound wall) with a gatehouse on the south. The accent is a recognition panel on the middle range's roof.

ruin._about: THE COMPLEX DESTROYED, PROPOSED in R1's language (decision strike-plan: the destroyed target as a ruin, crater and smoke column, no fire; the tower's ruin R1 is a working default, scripts/fx/fx_ruin.gd draw_remains): scorch (dirt stipple, thick in the middle, ink hatch on the shadow side), craters with a pale lip, the main hall roofless with its walls standing, the floor black and a torn piece of roof lying across the hole, the sheds in rubble heaps, a tank burst open, the chimney down, the fence partly gone. The smoke column is the effects layer's (kind military_complex would take it).

scorch_r_m._reason: the tower's scorch is 8 m round a 12 m target (R1); the complex is 6 to 7 times the size, so the scorch covers the main building and the nearest sheds without reaching the fence

craters._reason: a stick of four bombs leaves a line of craters; three are drawn, the biggest on the main building

crater_r_m._reason: R1's crater is 3.2 m; a 45 m blast reach cratered more than a mast's footing

fence_keep._reason: the share of fence panels still standing

rubble_pieces._reason: broken polygons round the main hall and in each shed's heap

wall_keep._reason: the share of the hall's wall stubs still standing

effects_size_frac._reason: the effects layer sizes the flash, the smoke burst, the plume and the smolder of a ruin by the unit's size_m (the tower's 12 m); the complex's size_m is 80, and a flash 40 m across and smoke puffs of 22 to 40 m would blanket the compound. The blast is the main building's (about 24 m): the effects are sized by this share of the 80 m (scripts/fx/fx_field.gd ruin)

roof_shaded._reason: the face of a roof turned from the sun: the one mix toward the shadow tint, 42 percent, as the village's houses use (draw_house)

concrete._reason: an apron or a floor of poured concrete: the village wall fill, a step off the paper

concrete_edge._reason: the slope tone of a wall (30 percent toward the shadow tint), used for the faces of low walls turned from the sun

yard._reason: packed earth under the stipple: the dirt colour at a faint alpha (the fields use 0.1 to 0.2)

ruin_char._reason: R1's ruin.char: a burnt floor, the dirt colour at 0.55

ruin_roof._reason: R1's ruin.roof: a torn piece of roof lying

ruin_shade._reason: R1's wreck.shade: the small shadow of a lying piece

pit._reason: R1's bomb.pit: the inside of a crater

lip._reason: R1's bomb.rim: the pale lip of a crater

heap._reason: a heap of coal or earth: the dirt colour at 0.5 under ink stipple
